gas-tx-caption: How gas moves in a message call, drawn as a fuel rig: the sender's pump fills a tank to the gas limit, the contract's engine burns what its code uses, and unused fuel flows back through a meter.
gas-tx-description: A transaction enters the world state. Its sender, an externally owned account, reserves a gas supply equal to the transaction's gas limit. A message carries the call to a contract account, whose EVM code runs and burns gas for each operation. When execution finishes, the unused gas, which is the gas limit minus the gas used, flows back to the externally owned account as a refund. If execution runs out of gas, all of the reserved gas is consumed, the contract's state changes are reverted, and nothing is returned.
gas-tx-readout-label: Gas for this example, in gas units
gas-tx-step-idle: Pick an example and send the transaction to follow its gas step by step.
gas-tx-step-enter: Step 1: the transaction enters the world state with a gas limit of {limit} gas.
gas-tx-step-reserve: Step 2: the externally owned account reserves the full {limit} gas as the gas supply.
gas-tx-step-execute: Step 3: the message reaches the contract account, and its EVM code runs and burns {used} gas.
gas-tx-step-execute-out-of-gas: Step 3: the EVM code needs more than {limit} gas, so it runs out of gas, burns all {limit} and fails.
gas-tx-step-return: Step 4: the {returned} unused gas flows back to the externally owned account as a refund.
gas-tx-step-revert: Step 4: the contract's state changes are reverted, and no gas is returned.
gas-tx-tooltip-deck: Drawn as the plate everything stands on: the state of every account.
gas-tx-tooltip-order: Drawn as a slip on the pump: a signed instruction that sets the gas limit.
gas-tx-tooltip-pump: Drawn as a pump: the externally owned account that pays for gas and gets unused gas back.
gas-tx-tooltip-tank: Drawn as a tank: the gas limit, reserved before execution starts and drained as gas burns.
gas-tx-tooltip-feed: Drawn as a pipe: the call itself, carried from the sender to the contract.
gas-tx-tooltip-engine: Drawn as an engine: the contract's EVM code burns gas for every operation it runs.
gas-tx-tooltip-return-line: Drawn as the return pipe: gas the call didn't use, flowing back to the sender.
gas-tx-tooltip-meter: Drawn as a meter: how much unused gas is returned to the sender.
gas-evm-caption: Where gas goes inside the EVM: the transaction first pays a fixed intrinsic cost, then every operation draws its own cost from the gas supply. Stack and memory work is cheap; writing to storage costs the most.
gas-evm-description: A gas supply feeds the EVM through a pipe. Before any code runs, the transaction pays 21,000 gas of intrinsic cost. Then the program counter steps through seven opcodes: two PUSH1 put 42 and 0 on the stack, MSTORE writes 42 to memory, two more PUSH1, then SSTORE writes 42 to a new storage slot, and STOP ends the run. Each opcode draws its cost from the supply; SSTORE alone costs 22,100 gas. With too little gas, execution runs out at SSTORE: all the gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-step-idle: Pick an example, then step through the code or run it.
gas-evm-step-intrinsic: Step 0: before any code runs, the transaction pays {intrinsic} gas of intrinsic cost.
gas-evm-step-push1: PUSH1 puts {value} on the stack: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-mstore: MSTORE writes 42 to memory, growing it by one word: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-sstore: SSTORE writes 42 to a new storage slot, the most expensive kind of write: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-stop: STOP ends the run: {used} gas used, {left} gas left to return.
gas-evm-step-out-of-gas: SSTORE needs {cost} gas but only {left} is left, so the call runs out of gas: all {limit} gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-tooltip-deck: The plate everything stands on: the state of every account. Only storage on it persists after the call.
gas-evm-tooltip-tank: The gas limit bought for the transaction. Intrinsic gas and every opcode draw from it.
gas-evm-tooltip-evm: The Ethereum Virtual Machine. Its program counter steps through the contract's code, one opcode at a time.
gas-evm-tooltip-stack: Short-lived working values. Pushing one costs 3 gas.
gas-evm-tooltip-memory: Scratch space for the call, cleared when it ends. Cheap, but growing it costs a little extra.
gas-evm-tooltip-storage: The contract's persistent state. Writing a new slot costs 22,100 gas, far more than anything else here.
tx-apply-caption: Applying a transaction: a signed transaction moves the world state from t to t+1. Bob sends Alice 1 ETH and pays a fee, which is split between a burn and a tip to the validator.
tx-apply-description: The world state is a plate with two accounts on it, Bob's (the sender) and Alice's (the recipient), joined by a pipe. Step 1: Bob signs a transaction sending Alice {value} and submits it. Step 2: {value} flows from Bob's account to Alice's. Step 3: the {fee} fee leaves Bob's account and splits at a junction: the {burned} base fee is burned, and the {tip} tip goes to the validator. Step 4: Bob's nonce goes up by one, and the world state becomes t+1: Bob has {sent} less, Alice has {value} more.
tx-apply-step-idle: Apply the transaction to follow how it changes the world state, step by step.
tx-apply-step-submit: Step 1: Bob signs a transaction sending Alice {value} and submits it.
tx-apply-step-value: Step 2: {value} flows from Bob's account to Alice's.
tx-apply-step-fee: Step 3: the {fee} fee splits: the {burned} base fee is burned and the {tip} tip goes to the validator.
tx-apply-step-commit: Step 4: Bob's nonce goes up by one, and the world state becomes t+1: Bob has {sent} less, Alice has {value} more.
tx-apply-tooltip-deck: Every account's balance and nonce. Each valid transaction moves it from one state to the next.
tx-apply-tooltip-sender: Bob's externally owned account. It pays the value and the fee, and its nonce counts its transactions.
tx-apply-tooltip-recipient: Alice's account. It receives the value.
tx-apply-tooltip-slip: The signed transaction: recipient, value, gas limit, fees and the sender's nonce.
tx-apply-tooltip-pipe: Carries the value from sender to recipient. The fee branches off at the junction.
tx-apply-tooltip-burn: The base fee (gas used × base fee) is burned: removed from circulation for good.
tx-apply-tooltip-tip: The priority fee (gas used × priority fee) goes to the validator who includes the transaction.
evm-zones-caption: What survives a call: the EVM's parts sit in three zones. Machine state is cleared when the call ends, the code never changes, and only writes to storage remain.
evm-zones-description: A plate (world state) carries the EVM on a plinth (machine state) and, apart from it, the account's storage. The plinth holds the gas available, the stack and memory; the EVM's code is a strip on its front, with the program counter as the lit cell. Step 1: the code is loaded, and it is immutable. Step 2: the call runs: values go on the stack, a word is written to memory, and gas drains. Step 3: SSTORE writes a value to a storage slot. Step 4: the call ends: the stack, memory and remaining gas are cleared, the code is unchanged, and the storage write remains.
evm-zones-step-idle: Run the call to see which parts of the EVM keep their contents when it ends.
evm-zones-step-load: Step 1: the contract's code is loaded into the EVM. Code is immutable: no call can change it.
evm-zones-step-run: Step 2: the call runs. The program counter steps through the code, values go on the stack, memory fills and gas drains.
evm-zones-step-store: Step 3: SSTORE writes a value to a storage slot in the account's storage, part of the world state.
evm-zones-step-end: Step 4: the call ends. Machine state is cleared, the code is unchanged, and the storage write remains.
evm-zones-tooltip-deck: The state of every account, kept from block to block.
evm-zones-tooltip-machine: The program counter, stack, memory and gas available: the EVM's working state during one call.
evm-zones-tooltip-evm: The contract's bytecode. The program counter steps through it one opcode at a time.
evm-zones-tooltip-tank: The gas left for this call. What remains at the end is returned.
evm-zones-tooltip-stack: Short-lived working values, up to 1,024 deep.
evm-zones-tooltip-memory: Scratch space for the call, cleared when it ends.
evm-zones-tooltip-storage: The contract's own key-value store. Writes made here outlast the call.
